sections.heading: Features
items: SDK improvements and bug fixes contributed by the Elastic team before the changes are available in OpenTelemetry repositories.
Optional features that can enhance OpenTelemetry data that is being sent to Elastic.
Elastic-specific processors that ensure optimal compatibility when exporting OpenTelemetry signal data to an Elastic backend like an Elastic Observability deployment.

Preconfigured collection of tracing and metrics signals, applying some opinionated defaults, such as which sources are collected by default. For example, the OpenTelemetry protocol (OTLP) exporter is enabled by default.
Built-in support for asynchronous data transmission, reducing request latency
Out-of-the-box auto-instrumentation — no need to modify your code. EDOT PHP takes care of enabling telemetry collection automatically.
Additional runtime features such as automatic root span creation, URL grouping, and inferred spans to provide richer and more structured trace data with minimal setup.
Compatibility with APM Agent Central Configuration to modify the settings of the EDOT PHP agent without having to restart the application.
notes: In addition to all the features of OpenTelemetry PHP, with EDOT PHP you have access to the following:

sections.heading: Technologies supported by EDOT PHP
sections.text: EDOT PHP is a [distribution](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/distributions/) of OpenTelemetry PHP. It inherits all the [supported](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/opentelemetry/compatibility/nomenclature) technologies of the OpenTelemetry PHP.
notes: Note - Understanding auto-instrumentation scope
Auto-instrumentation automatically captures telemetry for the frameworks and libraries listed on this page. However, it cannot instrument:
Custom or proprietary frameworks and libraries
Closed-source components without instrumentation support
Application-specific business logic
If your application uses technologies not covered by auto-instrumentation, you have two options:
1. **Native OpenTelemetry support** — Some frameworks and libraries include built-in OpenTelemetry instrumentation provided by the vendor.
2. **Manual instrumentation** — Use the [OpenTelemetry API](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/php/instrumentation/) to add custom spans, metrics, and logs for unsupported components.

sections.heading: EDOT Collector and Elastic Stack versions
sections.text: EDOT PHP sends data through the OpenTelemetry protocol (OTLP). While OTLP ingest works with later 8.16+ versions of the EDOT Collector, for full support use either [EDOT Collector](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/edot-collector) versions 9.x or [Elastic Cloud Serverless](https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/deploy/elastic-cloud/serverless) for OTLP ingest.
notes: Note
Ingesting data from EDOT SDKs through EDOT Collector 9.x into Elastic Stack versions 8.18+ is supported.
Refer to [EDOT SDKs compatibility](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/opentelemetry/compatibility/sdks) for support details.

sections.heading: PHP versions
sections.text: EDOT PHP supports PHP versions 8.1 to 8.5.
notes: Unlike the OpenTelemetry PHP agent, EDOT PHP supports extension-level instrumentation starting from PHP 8.1. This allows you to capture detailed traces from libraries such as cURL, PDO, and MySQLi even in PHP 8.1 environments.

sections.heading: Truly zero-config auto-instrumentation
sections.text: Unlike the OpenTelemetry PHP agent, EDOT PHP works fully automatically. There is no need to modify your application code, add Composer packages, or adjust deployment scripts. Once the system package is installed, EDOT PHP automatically detects your application and injects the instrumentation code at runtime, without requiring manual integration.
notes: Appears under the "Additional features and improvements" heading (https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/opentelemetry/edot-sdks/php/supported-technologies#additional-features-and-improvements).

sections.heading: Automatic Root/Transaction Span
sections.text: EDOT PHP automatically creates the root span for each incoming request, providing a consistent entry point for trace data without requiring manual instrumentation.
notes: Appears under the "Additional features and improvements" heading (https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/opentelemetry/edot-sdks/php/supported-technologies#additional-features-and-improvements).

sections.heading: Root/Transaction Span URL Grouping
sections.text: Transaction spans are grouped by URL patterns to reduce cardinality and improve readability in dashboards and trace views.
notes: Appears under the "Additional features and improvements" heading (https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/opentelemetry/edot-sdks/php/supported-technologies#additional-features-and-improvements).

sections.heading: Inferred Spans
sections.text: EDOT PHP automatically detects and generates spans for common operations like database queries or HTTP calls, even when no manual instrumentation is present.
notes: Appears under the "Additional features and improvements" heading (https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/opentelemetry/edot-sdks/php/supported-technologies#additional-features-and-improvements).

sections.heading: Attribute-based instrumentation
sections.text: EDOT PHP can automatically create spans from PHP 8.1 attributes (`#[WithSpan]`, `#[SpanAttribute]`) without writing instrumentation code. This feature is deactivated by default. Activate it by setting `OTEL_PHP_ATTR_HOOKS_ENABLED=true`. For details, refer to [Attribute-based instrumentation](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/opentelemetry/edot-sdks/php/attribute-instrumentation).
notes: Appears under the "Additional features and improvements" heading (https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/opentelemetry/edot-sdks/php/supported-technologies#additional-features-and-improvements).

sections.heading: PHP runtime metrics
sections.text: EDOT PHP automatically exports PHP runtime metrics — memory usage, garbage collection cycles, and peak memory — via the native async OTLP transport. EDOT PHP requires no configuration to emit these metrics. It starts exporting as soon as it loads.
notes: Appears under the "Additional features and improvements" heading (https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/opentelemetry/edot-sdks/php/supported-technologies#additional-features-and-improvements).

sections.heading: Asynchronous data sending
sections.text: Telemetry data is sent in the background to avoid impacting application performance. This ensures minimal latency and efficient resource usage.
notes: Note
EDOT PHP supports background data transmission (non-blocking export), but only when the exporter is set to `http/protobuf` (OTLP over HTTP), which is the default configuration.
If you change the exporter or the transport protocol, for example to gRPC or another format, telemetry will be sent synchronously, potentially impacting request latency.
